comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `hasAnyReportedUsage` is exported but has no caller**

`hasAnyReportedUsage` is barrel-exported public API, but nothing in `lib/` calls it — only its own test does. Its doc justifies it via E1 ("worth the caller's once-per-model note"), but that once-per-model note is not implemented anywhere in this PR (neither the executor nor the CLI stamps a "this provider never reports usage" hint anywhere).

Two options:
- wire the consumer this PR's doc promises (e.g. a one-time dim line when a child ran ≥N boundaries estimate-only while a registry entry marked the window verified — the exact gh-112 confusion shape), or
- keep the function but drop it from the barrel until a caller exists, so the public API surface (gh-1232 append-only policy) doesn't grow a speculative export.

Not blocking — dead-but-tested public helpers are cheap — but the barrel is append-only by policy, so exporting before the consumer exists is the wrong order.

comments.author: ai-teammate
ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: second hand-rolled Model copy — consider one shared helper**

`withRegisteredContextWindow` rebuilds `Model` field-by-field (18 fields) to swap one value. This is the second hand-copy of the full field list in the codebase (`_replaceModelLimits` in `provider_models.dart` is the first); `Model` has no `copyWith`, so the next field added to `Model` (they do get added — `timeoutScopeLabel`, `capabilityNotes`, `connectTimeout`, `streamIdleTimeout` are all recent) must be remembered in **two** hand-copies plus anywhere else this pattern lands, or it is silently dropped (the analyzer cannot catch a missing named argument on a constructor that doesn't require it).

Cheapest insurance while you are here: add `Model copyWith({int? contextWindow})` (or a focused `withContextWindow(int)`) next to the class and use it in both sites — then the field list lives exactly once, next to the class it mirrors.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "smol summarizer resolves the same number" claim is not implemented**

The registry's header doc says "main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx meter resolve the same number" — but the smol summarizer never touches the registry: `_compactChildIfNeeded` passes `rolesResolver?.resolveRole(smolModelRole)` straight into `AutoCompactorSources(smolModel:)` unwrapped, and the CLI's main compaction wiring does the same. So a smol model whose catalog window is wrong (exactly the copilot-1M-vs-256k-kimi shape the diff's own `_refreshModelCache` comment describes) still mis-bounds the #729 checkpoint payload budget and the structured engine's `summarizerWindow` — the same class of bug this ticket fixes for children.

Either scope the claim ("children and the meter" — the meter agrees via the mutated main model, which is worth saying explicitly too, since it does not literally read the registry either), or wrap the smol resolution with `withRegisteredContextWindow` once detections for that identity get published. As written, the doc promises a consumer that does not exist.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the forced latch grows without bound and never resets after a child is disposed**

`_forcedObservedAt` is keyed by child id and never evicted — not when a child completes, aborts, or is torn down. Retained children already live for the whole session, so this is one stale int per child at worst (bounded, cosmetic), but every other per-child map in this class (`_childSessions`, `_childSessionWrites`, `_flushCursor`-style state) gets cleaned on the dispose path; the latch is the one that does not. Adding it to the same cleanup keeps the "everything about a child dies with the child" invariant obvious to the next reader.

Also worth one clarifying word in the latch comment: the reset branch (`!decision.observedTriggered && observed < latch`) lowers the anchor but leaves the latch non-null — that is what makes the next re-crossing strictly-greater and re-armed, which took me a second read to confirm. A half-line ("reset = lower the anchor, keep the latch armed") would save it.

# Thread 1 — forWindow parity claim vs the formula (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart`)

Fixed by taking your option A: the floor is now the **exact legacy curve**, not the truncated one.

**Commit** `7d4a9db624` — `forWindow` builds

```dart
final legacyReserve = min(16384, max(1024, window ~/ 4));   // the full legacy curve
var reserveTokens  = min(65536, max(window ~/ 16, legacyReserve));
```

so the reserve rides the byte-identical legacy line through the whole band you tabled and only
switches to the proportional term where `window/16` overtakes it (≥ 262,144). Your rows now hold
at parity:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | parity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 5,120 | 5,120 | ✓ |
| 32,768 | 8,192 | 8,192 | ✓ |
| 65,536 | 16,384 | 16,384 | ✓ |
| 131,072 | 16,384 | 16,384 | ✓ |
| 200,000 | 16,384 | 16,384 | ✓ (window/16 = 12,500 loses the max) |

**Tests** (`test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`, UT-2 group): the legacy-parity group now pins
the mid-band rows explicitly — `forWindow(20480) == 5120`, `forWindow(32768) == 8192`,
`forWindow(65536) == 16384`, `forWindow(131072) == 16384`, `forWindow(262144) == 16384` — plus a
sweep asserting `new trigger <= legacy trigger` across the 8k–2M range, and the mirrored
`context_pressure_test.dart` comments were corrected to the same curve. The doc comment on
`forWindow` now states the real crossover (legacy term dominates below 262,144, proportional above).
Estimate-only (E1) providers therefore compact **no later than before** everywhere, as claimed.

# Thread 6 — the "smol summarizer resolves the same number" claim (`lib/src/compaction/context_window_registry.dart` header)

Implemented the consumer rather than scoping the claim down — the header now tells the truth.

**Commit** `befb7b93bf` — two gaps kept smol on the stale catalog value, both closed:

1. `_compactChildIfNeeded` (`task_executor.dart`) now wraps the roles-resolved smol model with the
   shared registry swap before handing it to `AutoCompactorSources`:

   ```dart

       ? null
       : withRegisteredContextWindow(smol.model, contextWindowRegistry),
   ```

   so the #729 checkpoint payload budget and the structured engine's `summarizerWindow` derive

2. `FallbackStreamFunction` (the roles chain) discarded the `StreamFunction` contract's caller
   model — every attempt dialed `ChainEntry.model` verbatim, so even a correctly patched caller
   model still dialed the stale catalog window. A caller whose model is the **same identity**
   (provider/modelId/baseUrl per `ModelWindowKey`) now dials with the caller's window; a different
   identity keeps the entry model, leaving failover semantics untouched. The CLI's main compaction
   wiring rides the same fix (its registry-patched main model now reaches the provider dial).

**Tests**: `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — "compaction LLM calls ride the smol
model WITH the registered window, not the stale catalog one" — publishes 478,000 for the smol
identity over a stale 400 catalog entry and asserts every judge/checkpoint call the child
compactor makes carries the registered window (and the transcript is fat enough that the
structured engine's hide pass genuinely runs, so the assertion is not vacuous).
`test/model_roles/fallback_stream_test.dart` pins the chain-level contract: same-identity caller
window honored, different-identity caller ignored.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Thread 7 — the forced latch grows without bound / reset semantics (`lib/src/task/task_executor.dart`)

Two halves — one doc fix applied, one eviction declined with the reason spelled out.

**The comment** (commit `409d83c480`): the latch comment now says exactly what you asked it to
say — reset **lowers the anchor while keeping the latch armed**, which is what makes the next
re-crossing strictly-greater and re-armed.

**The eviction**: I checked the dispose path you referenced, and there isn't one — not for the
latch, and not for any other per-child map in the class. `_childSessions`, `_childSessionWrites`,
and the flush-cursor state are never `.remove()`d either: retained children live for the whole
session **by design** (the E4 resume guards exist precisely so a completed child can be resumed,
and a resumed child keeps its id and therefore must keep its anchor — evicting the latch on
completion would let the first over-line observation after a resume re-force a pass the pre-dispose
anchor had already reacted to). A per-child cleanup event that the other maps "get cleaned on"
does not exist in this class, so adding one for the latch alone would not converge with them —
it would diverge.

The bounded cost you note (one stale int per child, dying with the `TaskExecutor` instance) is the
accurate model, and the comment now states that lifetime explicitly ("the anchor lives for the
child's whole retained lifetime … it dies with the executor rather than at some child-end event
that does not exist"). If a real per-child disposal pass is ever added (child teardown + mailbox
drain), the latch map should join it in the same change — but that is a class-wide lifecycle
feature, not a one-line fix here.
